title: Nutrition risque dépistage 2002 (NRS-2002)
formula:
**Initial Screening:** If “Yes” to any, proceed to Final Screening.

| BMI <20.5 kg/m² | Yes / No |
| --- | --- |
| Weight loss within 3 months | Yes / No |
| Reduced dietary intake in the last week | Yes / No |
| ICU patient | Yes / No |

**Final Screening:** addition of the selected points.

| | | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nutritional impairment | None | 0 points |
| Mild: weight loss >5% in 3 months or food intake <50–75% of normal requirement in the preceding week | 1 point | |
| Moderate: weight loss >5% in 2 months or BMI 18.5–20.5 plus impaired general condition or food intake 25–60% of normal requirement in preceding week | 2 points | |
| Severe: weight loss >5% in 1 month (>15% in 3 months) or BMI <18.5 plus impaired general condition or food intake 0–25% of normal requirement in preceding week | 3 points | |
| Severity of disease | Normal nutritional requirement | 0 points |
| Hip fracture, chronic illness (may have acute complications, e.g. cirrhosis or COPD), chronic dialysis, diabetes, cancer | 1 point | |
| Major abdominal surgery, stroke, severe pneumonia, hematologic malignancy | 2 points | |
| Head injury, bone marrow transplant, ICU patient with [APACHE](nabda:calc.apache-ii-score\) >10 | 3 points | |
| Age | <70 years | 0 points |
| ≥70 years | 1 point | |

how_to_use.why: Recommended by[American College of Gastroenterology (ACG) gudelines for nutrition therapy](https://www.mdcalc.com/guidelines/acg/nutrition-therapy-adult-hospitalized-patient).
how_to_use.when:
- Hospitalized patients at risk for malnutrition.
- For ICU patients, the [NUTRIC Score](nabda:calc.nutrition-risk-critically-ill-nutric-score) is a more widely validated risk predictor.

next_steps.advice: Consider nutrition consult in patients at risk for malnutrition.

more_info:
Interpretation:

| NRS-2002 | Risk group | Recommendation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0-3 | Low risk | Re-screen weekly |
| 4 | At risk | Initiate nutritional care plan (food, oral supplements, tube feeding, and/or parenteral nutrition as appropriate) |
| 5-7 | High risk | Initiate early intervention nutritional care plan |

From[ASPEN guidelines 2016](https://www.nutritioncare.org/uploadedFiles/01_Site_Directory/Guidelines_and_Clinical_Resources/EN_Pathway/McClave_et_al-2016-Journal_of_Parenteral_and_Enteral_Nutrition.pdf).
medium_description: Predicts risque de malnutrition dans hospitalized patients, recommended par[ACG guidelines](https://www.mdcalc.com/guidelines/acg/nutrition-therapy-adult-hospitalized-patient).
